name: Ahaz
bio:
Ahaz succeeded his father Jotham as king of Judah after Jotham was buried in the City of David (2 Kings 15:38).

## 📖 Core Story: Syro-Ephraimite Siege, and Tribute to Assyria

Ahaz reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem but did not do right like his ancestor David; he walked in the ways of Israel's kings, even making his own son pass through fire in pagan sacrifice, and offered sacrifices at the high places and under every green tree. Rezin, king of Syria, and Pekah, king of Israel, besieged Jerusalem but couldn't overcome Ahaz, though Rezin recovered Elath for Syria and drove out the Jews there. Ahaz sent to Tiglath-Pileser, king of Assyria, calling himself his servant and son, and sent him silver and gold from the temple and palace as tribute, begging rescue from Syria and Israel. Assyria obliged, attacking Damascus, deporting its people, and killing Rezin (2 Kings 16:1-9).

After visiting Damascus to meet Tiglath-Pileser, Ahaz saw a pagan altar there and sent its design back to Urijah the priest, who built a matching altar in the temple before Ahaz returned. Ahaz began using this new altar for all the regular sacrifices, demoting the LORD's own bronze altar, and stripped various bronze temple fixtures, sending some of them away to please the king of Assyria (2 Kings 16:10-18). Ahaz died and was buried in the City of David, and his son Hezekiah succeeded him (2 Kings 16:19-20).
